findings.summary: The new tests pin only the positive arm of the fenced/close distinction -- that a fenced commit throws FencedException -- and no test anywhere asserts that the deliberate-close refusal is NOT a FencedException, so the exact confusion the task exists to remove survives once it moves from the message to the type.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutate LocalSequencer.commitAll's closed branch (LocalSequencer.java:417-422) to throw new FencedException(...) with the identical message. Every test stays green: LocalSequencerTest.committingAfterCloseFailsRatherThanSilentlySucceeding asserts only isInstanceOf(IOException.class) plus hasMessageContaining("released its lease at epoch 1"), and the deliberate-close test in LocalSequencerRenewTest asserts isInstanceOf(IOException.class), hasMessageContaining("released its lease") and hasMessageNotContaining("fenced") -- a FencedException satisfies all four. No isNotInstanceOf/isExactlyInstanceOf assertion exists anywhere in sequencer/src/test. Concretely: pod1 is closed on SIGTERM, an in-flight commit hits the closed branch and under the mutation gets a FencedException; the M5.6 caller that forwards on exactly instanceof FencedException then treats a deliberate shutdown as a lost term and forwards/re-elects on the way out -- the defect the task names, reintroduced at the type level with the suite unable to see it. Killing it needs one assertion on the close refusal, e.g. isNotInstanceOf(FencedException.class).
